name: With the Bite In
tagline: Said straight, they'd stop you. So you make them laugh.
epigraph: A song made rum and Coca-Cola famous. The song was never really about the drink.
glassware: a tall glass, filled with ice
language_row: Wren's resonance: ready (v2; carried to v3 in r5). Guest text 4-gram clean against every pour (Wren r3–r5). Gendered pronouns in y1–y3 refer to Lord Invader only. History about half of yours (0.499).

names_note: With the Bite In (Wren; all three by r4). Also considered: Slipped Past (Tomás), Past the Censors; Actual Size and Down to Size struck (Down the Line owns size; "cut down to size" leans to humiliation).
open_items: Contains nuts, on the safe side: Tomás reclassified the shared coca_cola row in dps-tools/data/ingredients.json as nuts, because two published historical 7X formulas (Beal 1979, Pemberton via Pendergrast) list nutmeg oil; Coca-Cola denies they are the formula and today's recipe is secret. The same row feeds innocent-creator (The Way It Felt), whose file still says veto-free: a note for Robin, not edited here. The plan's "Subverter stays veto-free" no longer holds.
The plan's lead, H. L. Mencken, was struck by Wren in r1: the deliberate arrest is Can't Watch's shape, and his posthumous diary punches down (point 5, the ending after the page).

The tune was Lionel Belasco's ("L'Année Passée", 1906), the plaintiff was Khan, and the lyric case was 1947 (the melody case 1948): so "his words", "a court found that Lord Invader had written the words", never "he sued", "he won" or "his song". No dollar figure ($132,000 vs $150,000) and no death year (1961 vs 1962).

The ending is told with its cost: paid seven years late and "always short of money" after (Cowley). Yankee Dollar is used on its chorus only, Crisis in Arkansas on the bow-tie joke only. Kept out: the women in the lyric, God Made Us All (credited to Lord Pretender), the unreleased Pepsi-Cola jingle (dossier only).

Angostura 1919's 40% is the maker's figure from Tomás's own knowledge, unread on a label; swept 37.5–43%, in range. Cost about £35–40 / $35–40 a bottle, unsourced. Substitute: a column-distilled aged rum, not spiced, about 40% (not Trinidadian). No Trinidad rum style is on a page.
